items.title: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
items.text: Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
items.text: Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
items.text: Brooks, who is on injured reserve due to a groin injury, has eight days to be activated or lost for the season. The 23-year-old back practiced in full last week all three times only to not be activated. It would be great news for Chuba Hubbard if this continued, as the team has shown little interest in using Etienne in a real role in the backfield. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
items.text: Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
items.text: After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. items.title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
items.text: It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
items.text: After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
items.text: Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
items.text: The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season.
